problem: Find the first term of an arithmetic series if its $5$th term is $-0.28$ and the sum of the first $12$ terms of the series is $-12.$

feedback.problem: If the $9$th term of an arithmetic series is $\frac{46}{3}$ and the sum of the first $15$ terms is $200,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given one term of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=15$ and ${S}_{N}=200$ into the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d) \\ 200 & =\frac{15}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(15-1)d) \\ 400 & =15(2{a}_{1}+14d) \\ \frac{400}{15} & =2{a}_{1}+14d \\ \frac{80}{3} & =2{a}_{1}+14d.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we can write an equation for the $9$th term of the arithmetic series and substitute in its known value:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)d \\ {a}_{9} & ={a}_{1}+(9-1)d \\ \frac{46}{3} & ={a}_{1}+8d\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we obtain the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}\frac{46}{3}={a}_{1}+8d \\ \frac{80}{3}=2{a}_{1}+14d\end{aligned}
$$

To solve this system, we multiply the first equation by $-2$ and add the result to the second equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{92}{3} & =-2{a}_{1}-16d \\ \frac{80}{3} & =2{a}_{1}+14d \\ -\frac{12}{3} & =-2d \\ d & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $d=2$ into the first equation, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{46}{3} & ={a}_{1}+8d \\ \frac{46}{3} & ={a}_{1}+8(2) \\ \frac{46}{3} & ={a}_{1}+16 \\ \frac{46}{3} & ={a}_{1}+\frac{48}{3} \\ {a}_{1} & =-\frac{2}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
